classification.difficultyReason: Recognise local and global extrema and horizontal points of inflection directly from unscaled graphs.

content.prompt:
In the diagrams below, classify each labelled point as a:
Global maximum, global minimum, local maximum, local minimum, horizontal inflection.

spec.description: Unscaled curve with local maximum A left of the vertical axis and local minimum B right of it; continuation arrows descend left and ascend right.
spec.mathematics: The curve is unbounded below and above; A and B are local extrema.
spec.answerVisibility: Labels and filled points are supplied; classifications are hidden.

answer.worked: A is higher than the nearby points on both sides. The curve rises higher elsewhere, so A is a local maximum.
B is lower than the nearby points on both sides. The left branch continues lower, so B is a local minimum.

spec.description: Unscaled graph between dashed vertical domain boundaries, with C above the axis, D and E below it, and closed right endpoint F lower than D.
spec.mathematics: C is the highest point on the shown domain; F is the lowest. D and E are interior local extrema.
spec.answerVisibility: Domain boundaries, points and labels are supplied; classifications are hidden.

answer.worked: C has the largest function value over the entire shown domain, so C is the global maximum.
D is lower than nearby points on both sides, but F is lower. Therefore D is a local minimum.
E is higher than nearby points on both sides, but C is higher. Therefore E is a local maximum.
The included endpoint F has the smallest function value over the entire shown domain, so F is the global minimum.

spec.description: Curve begins at the axes' intersection, rises to G, then descends through a horizontal tangent at H and continues downward.
spec.mathematics: G is the highest point. The curve decreases through the stationary point H, changing concavity there.
spec.answerVisibility: Filled points and labels are supplied; classifications are hidden.

answer.worked: G has the largest function value over the entire shown domain, so G is the global maximum.
The tangent at H is horizontal. The curve changes concavity and continues decreasing through H, so H is a horizontal point of inflection.

spec.description: Curve descends from an upper-left arrow through horizontal inflection I, reaches minimum J, and rises through the axes' intersection to an upper-right arrow.
spec.mathematics: I has a horizontal tangent with continuing descent and a change of concavity. J is the lowest point; both ends rise.
spec.answerVisibility: Filled points and labels are supplied; classifications are hidden.

answer.worked: The tangent at I is horizontal. The curve changes concavity and continues decreasing through I, so I is a horizontal point of inflection.
J has the smallest function value over the entire shown domain, so J is the global minimum.
